q: The electric potentials of charged conductors are expressed relative to the electric potential of the ____.
e: The earth serves as the universal reference point for zero electric potential in practical applications.

q: The earth is a ____ of enormous size.
e: The earth acts as a massive electrical conductor capable of accepting or supplying electrons without significantly changing its overall potential.

q: When compared to the size of the earth the number of electrons gained or lost by it is very small so that the ____ of the earth does not change.
e: The earth's vast size means that typical charge transfers have a negligible effect on its overall net charge.

q: The electric potential of a conductor becomes ____ when it is connected to the earth.
e: Earthing (or grounding) a conductor equalizes its potential with that of the earth, which is defined as zero.

q: Suppose a positively charged body is connected to the earth as shown in Figure 9.11(a), electrons flow ____.
c: from the earth to the body
e: Electrons are attracted from the earth to neutralize the positive charge on the body.

q: In both cases, the electron flow takes place until the sphere has ____.
e: Charge transfer continues until the potential difference is eliminated and the object is neutralized.
